methodologyNotes: Roster covers twelve electronic (sound-amplifying, gunshot-compressing) shooting earmuffs from Walker's, Howard Leight/Honeywell, 3M Peltor, AXIL, ISOtunes, Pro Ears, Caldwell, and MSA Sordin, verified 2026-08-11 against manufacturer product pages and corroborated by major retailer/review listings (Amazon, Walmart, OpticsPlanet, Bass Pro, Cabela's, Midway USA, Ammo Bros). Two adversarial corrections were made to the seed list: (1) "Axil GS Extreme 2.0" is an in-ear Bluetooth earbud product (goaxil.com/products/gx-extreme), not an over-ear earmuff, so it was replaced with AXIL's actual current over-ear electronic model, the MXII PRO, as the true product-category match from the same brand; (2) "Caldwell E-Max Shadows" is likewise an in-ear Bluetooth earplug product (caldwellshooting.com E-Max line), not an earmuff, so it was replaced with Caldwell's actual over-ear electronic model, the E-Max Low Profile. A third seed item, "ClearArmor 141001," was dropped rather than substituted: cross-referencing Amazon's own listing (SNR-only rating, no stated microphone/amplifier/battery spec), ClearArmor's product copy ("noise suppression is not electronic"), and independent reviews confirms the 141001 is a purely passive earmuff with no electronics, batteries, or ambient-sound amplification, so it does not belong in an electronic-earmuffs dataset and no verified electronic ClearArmor model could be located to substitute in its place; the roster was left at twelve verified entries rather than include a mismatched or unverified thirteenth. Fields left null (amplification cutoff time, microphone directionality, cushion type, foldable design, weight) reflect specs genuinely not published or not independently confirmed by the fetched sources for that exact model, rather than being inferred by analogy to sibling products. accessedAt 2026-08-11 throughout.

products.name: Walker's Razor Slim Electronic Earmuff
products.priceNote: Representative current street price (varies $30-$45 across camo/color SKUs); Walker's does not display a single fixed MSRP across all colorways

specs.Battery type & runtime: 2x AAA; ~40 hrs at high volume, ~80 hrs at low volume
specs.Cushion type: low-profile sound-dampening composite ear cups (gel-hybrid replacement pads sold separately)

products.provenance: Walker's Game Ear's own Razor Slim product page confirms NRR 23, two hi-gain omnidirectional microphones, sound-activated compression (SAC) of 0.02 seconds (20 ms), 2x AAA batteries, external battery door, and the ultra-low-profile folding composite housing. Battery runtime (40 hrs high / 80 hrs low) corroborated on Amazon listings. No manufacturer- or retailer-published net weight in ounces was located, so weight is left null rather than estimated.

products.name: Walker's XCEL 500BT Digital Electronic Muff with Voice Clarity and Bluetooth
products.priceNote: Representative current retail (OpticsPlanet/Bass Pro); frequently discounted ~25-30% off list
products.provenance: Walker's own XCEL 500BT page confirms NRR 26, Bluetooth streaming/calls, four listening modes (Universal, Speech Clarity, High Frequency, Power Boost), next-gen variable Dynamic Sound Suppression, and 2/4/6-hr programmable auto-shutoff; 2x AAA battery power confirmed on Amazon. No fixed-ms compression figure or cushion-material spec is published for this model, so those fields are null rather than assumed from the (foldable, gel-cushioned) Razor Slim. This is a full-size, non-folding digital muff, distinct from the slim/folding Razor series, so foldable design is recorded as false. Weight taken from Walmart listing (2 lb package weight = 32 oz).

products.name: Howard Leight by Honeywell Impact Sport Sound Amplification Electronic Shooting Earmuff

specs.Battery type & runtime: 2x AAA; ~350 hrs; auto shut-off after 4 hrs

products.provenance: Honeywell's official Impact Sport product/spec sheet confirms NRR 22, built-in directional microphones that amplify ambient sound to a safe 82 dB and auto-cut above it, ~350-hr battery life on 2x AAA with 4-hr auto shut-off, and a compact folding design. No manufacturer-published compression reaction time in milliseconds was found (unlike Walker's stated 0.02 s SAC), so that field is left null. Weight (10.6 oz) is corroborated via a third-party Impact Sport/Impact Pro comparison (wcsafety.com) citing Honeywell's own listed figure.

products.name: Howard Leight by Honeywell Impact Pro High NRR Sound Amplification Electronic Earmuff

specs.Battery type & runtime: 2x AAA; ~350 hrs; auto shut-off after 4 hrs
specs.Cushion type: rubberized pressure-point ear seals, soft-padded headband

products.provenance: Honeywell's official Impact Pro page confirms NRR 30 (highest in the Impact line), directional microphones amplifying to a safe 82 dB with auto shut-off above that level, 2x AAA batteries with ~350-hr life and 4-hr auto shut-off, rugged rubberized pressure-point ear cups, and a soft-padded headband. Impact Pro is described only as physically larger than the folding Impact Sport, with no explicit fold/no-fold spec published, and no net weight in ounces was found on any fetched source, so both fields are left null rather than assumed by analogy to the Impact Sport.

products.name: 3M Peltor Sport Tactical 500 Smart Electronic Hearing Protector
products.priceNote: Current representative retail (Rifle Configurator/Amazon); ranges ~$170-$200 across retailers

specs.Battery type & runtime: 2x AA, or optional 3M Alpha 1100 Li-ion pack (USB-charged); ~8 hrs on the rechargeable pack

products.provenance: 3M's official Sport Tactical 500 page confirms NRR 26, Bluetooth wireless technology for calls/audio, dual power options (2x AA or the Alpha 1100 rechargeable Li-ion pack charged via the headset's micro-USB port, ~8-hr life), gunshot suppression via Dynamic Suppression Time, and Clear Voice Tracking. 3M's marketing materials describe stereo ambient-sound pickup without stating directional vs. omnidirectional in the fetched copy; omni is used as the commonly documented mic configuration for this model per independent reviews (thetruthaboutguns.com), noted here as moderate confidence. No fixed-ms compression time or cushion/fold specs were found in fetched sources, so those fields are null. Weight (14.9 oz with batteries) corroborated via soundscapehq.com's spec summary.

products.name: 3M Peltor Sport Tactical 300 Electronic Hearing Protector
products.priceNote: Current Walmart/Midway USA retail (TAC300-OTH); OpticsPlanet lists ~17% off a higher list price

specs.Battery type & runtime: 2x AA (not included), or optional 3M Alpha 1100 Li-ion pack (sold separately)

products.provenance: 3M's official Sport Tactical 300 page confirms NRR 24, Gunshot Recognition and Suppression Technology, Clear Voice Tracking, recessed microphones designed to reduce wind/fan noise, and dual power support (2x AA or the Alpha 1100 rechargeable pack, sold separately, same as the Tactical 500). No Bluetooth is offered on this model (confirmed by its absence from spec copy where the Tactical 500 explicitly lists it). Microphone directionality, compression time in ms, cushion material, foldability, and weight were not stated on any fetched source, so all are left null rather than inferred from the sibling Tactical 500.

products.name: AXIL TRACKR Electronic Earmuffs
products.provenance: AXIL's official TRACKR electronic-earmuff page confirms NRR 22, Sound Activated Compression with a 0.02-second (20 ms) reaction time, 40 dB gain, sweat/water resistance, and power from 2x included AAA batteries rated for about 8 hours. Note: earplugstore.com's separate listing for a passive TRACKR variant cites NRR 25, which applies to that non-electronic sibling model, not this electronic entry. Microphone directionality, cushion material, foldability, and net weight were not published on any fetched source, so those fields are null.

products.name: AXIL MXII PRO Bluetooth Electronic Earmuffs

specs.Battery type & runtime: Rechargeable Li-ion, USB-C; ~60 hrs hear-through, ~45 hrs music, ~40 hrs combined use
specs.Cushion type: replaceable ear cushions (material not specified by manufacturer)

products.provenance: SUBSTITUTED FROM SEED: the seed item "Axil GS Extreme 2.0" is an in-ear Bluetooth earbud/earplug product (goaxil.com/products/gx-extreme, IP65, 15-hr combined battery life), not an over-ear earmuff, so it does not belong in this earmuff dataset. AXIL's current flagship over-ear electronic model, the MXII PRO, was substituted as the correct product-category match from the same brand. AXIL's official page confirms NRR 22, Bluetooth 5.3 audio (single-device pairing, ~30 m range), SonicShieldX impulse filtering, IP65 water resistance, a built-in AXIL earplug storage compartment, and USB-C rechargeable battery life (~60 hrs hear-through / ~45 hrs music / ~40 hrs combined). No fixed-ms compression time, explicit mic directionality, foldability, or net weight figure was found on any fetched source, so those fields are null rather than assumed from the AXIL TRACKR.

products.name: ISOtunes Sport DEFY BT Electronic Shooting Earmuff

specs.Battery type & runtime: Rechargeable Li-ion; ~11 hrs on Bluetooth, or AAA backup batteries for ~22 hrs

products.provenance: ISOtunes' official DEFY BT page confirms NRR 25 (ANSI S3.19-1974 tested), Bluetooth 4.2 dual-device connectivity, Tactical Sound Control Technology enhancing hearing up to 8x while cutting off high-impact noise in under 2 milliseconds, SafeMax volume limiting to 85 dB, IPX4 water resistance, a vented headband, and memory foam ear cushions. Battery life (11 hrs rechargeable / 22 hrs on AAA backup) and weight (15.5 oz) corroborated via Cabela's and Canex listings. Microphone directionality and foldability were not stated on any fetched source, so those fields are null.

products.name: Pro Ears Gold II 26 Electronic Hearing Protection
products.priceNote: Manufacturer retail on proears.com ($199.99); frequently discounted lower at third-party retailers (Amazon)
products.provenance: Pro Ears' official Gold II 26 page and Amazon listing confirm NRR 26, Dynamic Level Sound Compression (DLSC) with an FSS 1.5-millisecond response time, up to 8x sound amplification, gel ear seals, per-cup independent volume control, a low-battery indicator, and power from 4x AAA batteries (not included). Made in USA per manufacturer copy. Microphone directionality, foldability, and net weight in ounces were not published on any fetched source, so those fields are null.

products.name: Caldwell E-Max Low Profile Electronic Hearing Protection
products.priceNote: Current retail (Midway USA / Walmart); ranges $30-$45 across colorways
products.provenance: SUBSTITUTED FROM SEED: the seed item "Caldwell E-Max Shadows" is an in-ear Bluetooth earplug product (caldwellshooting.com E-Max Shadows line, 23 dB NRR earbuds with a charging case), not an over-ear earmuff, so it does not belong in this earmuff dataset. Caldwell's over-ear electronic model, the E-Max Low Profile, was substituted as the correct product-category match from the same brand. Caldwell's official page and Amazon/Midway USA listings confirm NRR 23 (some SKUs/colorways listed 21-25 depending on retailer), two microphones that amplify ambient sound below 85 dB and cut off above it, an integrated audio input jack, 1.75 in. ear cup width, power from 2x AAA batteries (not included), and a 1.0 lb (16 oz) product weight. This base Low Profile SKU does not include Bluetooth, distinguishing it from a separately sold "Bluetooth" variant of the same product line. Microphone directionality, cushion material, and foldability were not stated on any fetched source, so those fields are null.

products.name: MSA Sordin Supreme Pro-X Electronic Earmuff
products.priceNote: Representative US authorized-dealer price (SRS Tactical / MasterBasser); premium editions with gel seals and leather headband run higher. Sordin sells only through distributors, not direct.
products.provenance: Sordin's official Supreme Pro-X page and MSA/dealer spec sheets confirm an ANSI S3.19 NRR of 18 dB (also independently certified to a higher EN352 SNR of 25 dB under the European standard — the two ratings use different test methods and are not directly comparable; NRR 18 is used here as the US-standard figure this dataset's spec key calls for), two splash-proof microphones reproducing ambient sound with output capped around 82 dB, IP67-rated electronics/battery compartment, 2x AAA batteries rated for 600+ hours, and gel ear seals available on premium editions (used as the representative cushion type). Weight (401 g including batteries, per MSA's own spec table) converts to 14.1 oz. Microphone directionality, exact compression time in ms, and foldability were not confirmed on any fetched source, so those fields are null.
